summary: This standards-track RFC extends RSVP-TE signaling to support label switched paths in GMPLS-controlled optical networks that use the flexible optical grid. This allows channels of varying widths to be set up in DWDM networks.

plainLanguage.summary: Fiber used to be sliced into fixed lanes. This lets lanes be wider or narrower as needed, and describes how to ask for them.

questions: how is slot width signaled in rsvp-te
subtitle: How RSVP-TE asks for optical channels of variable width in flexible-grid DWDM networks.

tldr.problem: Flexi-grid DWDM networks let each optical channel take a different amount of spectrum, but RSVP-TE had no way to carry the requested slot width in signaling.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines new C-Types for the SENDER_TSPEC and FLOWSPEC objects that carry a 16-bit value m, where the slot width is m * 12.5 GHz. The frequency position is carried in labels defined in RFC 7699.
tldr.outcome: LSPs can be signaled across flexible-grid networks, and the same traffic parameters can describe fixed-grid widths too. It adds no new security considerations beyond RFC 3473.

today: RFC 7792 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It works together with RFC 7698 and RFC 7699.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
A frequency grid is a reference set of allowed nominal central frequencies for WDM transmission. Fixed-grid channel spacing is chosen from 12.5 GHz, 25 GHz, 50 GHz, 100 GHz and integer multiples of 100 GHz. The ITU-T G.694.1 recommendation also defines flexible grids, using a frequency slot (the range allocated to one channel) and a slot width (the full width of that slot).

RFC 7698 gives the framework and control-plane requirements for GMPLS control of flexi-grid DWDM networks. This document adds the requirements and RSVP-TE extensions (building on RFC 3473) needed to set up LSPs in such networks.
sections.plainLanguage: Old fiber links came with a few fixed lane sizes. Flexi-grid lets lanes be custom sizes, and this document teaches the network to ask for them.

sections.title: Requirements for Signaling
sections.content:
An optical-spectrum LSP occupies a frequency slot. Finding a route and assigning that slot is called Routing and Spectrum Assignment (RSA). With centralized spectrum assignment, the slot is given in the RSVP-TE Path message at setup. With distributed spectrum assignment, the Path message carries only the slot width, and nodes pick the frequency while processing the messages.

The slot width is an end-to-end parameter, the equivalent of optical bandwidth, and MUST be carried in the signaling message. That tells nodes how much was requested (Path) and how much was allocated (Resv). The Resv message MUST also carry the central frequency hop by hop. Together, central frequency and slot width identify the frequency slot, from (central frequency minus half the width) to (central frequency plus half the width).

The head-end must be able to suggest or require the central frequency in a Path message, and for bidirectional LSPs the Path message MUST be able to specify the central frequency for the reverse direction.
sections.plainLanguage: To book a lane you must say how wide it is and where it sits. The width travels with the request, and the final position is confirmed on the way back.

sections.title: Slot Width and Central Frequency Rules
sections.content:
Per G.694.1, the nominal central frequency in THz is 193.1 + n * 0.00625, where n is zero or a positive or negative integer. The slot width in GHz is 12.5 * m, where m is a positive integer.

An implementation may support only a subset. The RFC's example limits central frequency granularity to 12.5 GHz by allowing only even values of n, and limits slot widths to 25 GHz by allowing only even values of m.
sections.plainLanguage: Positions and widths are counted in small steps, like tiles on a floor. You choose how many tiles wide your lane is and which tile it is centered on.

sections.title: The SSON Traffic Parameters
sections.content:
In RSVP-TE, SENDER_TSPEC in the Path message indicates the requested reservation and FLOWSPEC in the Resv message the actual one. The RFC defines new C-Types for both to carry Spectrum-Switched Optical Network (SSON) traffic parameters: SENDER_TSPEC is Class 12, C-Type 8, and FLOWSPEC is Class 9, C-Type 8.

The format is a 16-bit m followed by 16 reserved bits. The slot width is m * 12.5 GHz. The Reserved bits MUST be set to zero and ignored upon receipt.
sections.plainLanguage: The request form has one number: how many 12.5 GHz steps wide you want. The rest of the form is blank space that must stay empty.

sections.title: Labels, Fixed Grids and Procedures
sections.content:
Labels in flexi-grid networks are encoded as in RFC 7699, and can appear in any RSVP-TE object or sub-object that can carry a label. The m parameter forms part of the label as well as of the traffic parameters. A compound label, a concatenation of flexi-grid labels, is used when an LSP uses multiple slots.

Fixed-grid spacings (12.5 GHz, 25 GHz, 50 GHz, 100 GHz and integer multiples of 100 GHz) are all multiples of 12.5 GHz, so the same traffic parameters can express them. That allows common signaling for flexi-grid and legacy DWDM networks.

Signaling procedures are the same as those in RFC 7698 and RFC 7689, using the new TSpec, FlowSpec and label formats. Both distributed and centralized spectrum assignment can be applied.
sections.plainLanguage: The old fixed lane sizes are just special cases of the new scheme, so one kind of request form can serve both old and new networks.

sections.title: IANA, Management and Security
sections.content:
IANA allocated C-Type 8 under Class 9 (FLOWSPEC) as SSON FLOWSPEC and C-Type 8 under Class 12 (SENDER_TSPEC) as SSON SENDER_TSPEC, in the RSVP Parameters registry.

Manageability is largely unchanged, though protocol analysis tools, logging systems and MIB modules will need to support the new traffic parameters and label formats. The document introduces no new security considerations beyond RFC 3473, and points to RFC 5920 for GMPLS signaling security.
sections.plainLanguage: The new form number was officially registered, and nothing here makes the network less safe than before.

fields.name: m
fields.desc: A positive integer; slot width is m * 12.5 GHz.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: MUST be set to zero and ignored upon receipt.
